_meta.purpose: Canonical statutory lookup for the deterministic Legal Compliance Shield. Seed entries verified against primary sources and official gazettes on 2026-09-17. Reflects BNS, BNSS, BSA, IT Act, DPDP Act, and PMLA.
_meta.transition_note: BNS/BNSS/BSA replaced IPC/CrPC/Indian Evidence Act with effect from 1 July 2024.

BNS.name: Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023
BNS.full_title: The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 (Act No. 45 of 2023)

BNSS.name: Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023
BNSS.full_title: The Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (Act No. 46 of 2023)

BSA.name: Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023
BSA.full_title: The Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 (Act No. 47 of 2023)

IT Act.name: Information Technology Act, 2000
IT Act.full_title: The Information Technology Act, 2000 (Act No. 21 of 2000)

DPDP Act.name: Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023
DPDP Act.full_title: The Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 (Act No. 22 of 2023)

PMLA.name: Prevention of Money Laundering Act, 2002
PMLA.full_title: The Prevention of Money Laundering Act, 2002 (Act No. 15 of 2003)

sections.title: Cheating
sections.source: MHA official BNS text; BNS 318(4) = old IPC 420 (cheating and dishonestly inducing delivery of property); BNS 318(2) = old IPC 417
sections.mandatory_notes: Primary penal charging section for cyber fraud and dishonest inducement of funds.

sections.title: Cheating by personation
sections.source: MHA official BNS text; BNS 319 = old IPC 419
sections.mandatory_notes: Applies to impersonation of law enforcement, bank officials, or government authorities in digital arrest/phishing.

sections.title: Criminal breach of trust
sections.source: MHA official BNS text; BNS 316 = old IPC 406/409
sections.mandatory_notes: Applies where digital funds or assets were lawfully entrusted and dishonestly converted/misappropriated.

sections.title: Extortion
sections.source: MHA official BNS text; BNS 308 = old IPC 383-389
sections.mandatory_notes: Applicable in coercive cyber extortion, digital arrest threats, and sextortion schemes.

sections.title: Forgery
sections.source: MHA official BNS text; BNS 336(3) = old IPC 468 (forgery for purpose of cheating)
sections.mandatory_notes: Covers creation of forged digital documents, notices, warrants, or payment receipts.

sections.title: Forgery of valuable security, will, etc.
sections.source: MHA official BNS text; BNS 338 = old IPC 467
sections.mandatory_notes: Covers forgery of banking authorizations, bills of exchange, and valuable securities.

sections.title: Forged document or electronic record / Using as genuine
sections.source: MHA official BNS text; BNS 340(2) = old IPC 471 (using as genuine a forged document or electronic record)
sections.mandatory_notes: Applies when suspect fraudulently passes off altered or fake electronic records.

sections.title: Criminal conspiracy
sections.source: MHA official BNS text; BNS 61(1) defines conspiracy, BNS 61(2) = old IPC 120B punishment
sections.mandatory_notes: Invoked in multi-tiered cyber fraud operations involving mule networks and recruiters.

sections.title: Organized crime
sections.source: MHA official BNS text; new comprehensive provision
sections.mandatory_notes: Applies to continuing unlawful cyber-syndicates committing financial crimes.

sections.title: Seizure of property (including bank account freeze)
sections.source: MHA official BNSS text; Blue Sea Ventures v. State of AP (AP HC, 2025)
sections.mandatory_notes: MANDATORY JUDICIAL SAFEGUARD: Immediate reporting to the jurisdictional Magistrate is required. Freezing without magistrate intimation is legally invalid.

sections.title: Attachment, forfeiture or restoration of property
sections.mandatory_notes: Requires application to Court for attachment of proceeds of crime.

sections.title: Summons to produce document or other thing (electronic records)
sections.mandatory_notes: Expressly authorizes requisitioning electronic communications and digital records from service providers.

sections.title: Information in cognizable cases (FIR, Zero FIR & e-FIR)
sections.mandatory_notes: Mandates receipt of electronic information (e-FIR) and Zero FIR without jurisdictional denial.

sections.title: Police officer's power to investigate cognizable case
sections.mandatory_notes: Section 175(3) requires prior complaint recourse and affidavit for judicial investigation orders.

sections.title: Procedure when investigation cannot be completed in 24 hours (Custody & Remand)
sections.source: MHA official BNSS text; State of AP v. Suda Suresh (SC, 2026)
sections.mandatory_notes: 15 days maximum police custody may be availed in whole or in parts across the initial 40 or 60 day detention window.

sections.title: Admissibility of electronic or digital records
sections.mandatory_notes: Electronic records have the same legal status and enforceability as traditional paper documents.

sections.title: Proof of electronic records
sections.mandatory_notes: Outlines procedural requirements for electronic evidence production in judicial proceedings.

sections.title: Conditions for admissibility of electronic records & Certificate
sections.source: MHA official BSA gazette text; Indian Kanoon
sections.mandatory_notes: MANDATORY CERTIFICATE REQUIREMENTS: To admit secondary electronic evidence, certificate under 63(4) requires dual signatures (device operator + expert/custodian) and SHA-256 hash value.

sections.title: Cheating by personation using computer resource
sections.mandatory_notes: Core cyber offence: punishes cheating by personation by means of any computer resource or communication device.

sections.title: Identity theft
sections.mandatory_notes: Fraudulent or dishonest use of electronic signature, password, UPI credentials, or unique identification feature.

sections.title: Computer related offences
sections.mandatory_notes: Dishonestly or fraudulently committing any act referred to in Section 43 (unauthorized access, download, malware).

sections.title: Violation of privacy
sections.mandatory_notes: Capturing, publishing, or transmitting images of private area without consent.

sections.title: Cyber terrorism
sections.mandatory_notes: Threatening unity, integrity, or security of India by denying or damaging critical information infrastructure.

sections.title: Directions for interception, monitoring or decryption of information
sections.mandatory_notes: Requires statutory order from authorized competent authority (Home Secretary); unauthorized interception is illegal.

sections.title: Power to issue directions for blocking public access to computer resource
sections.mandatory_notes: Used for blocking fraudulent URLs, fake phishing portals, and illegal APK hosting sites.

sections.title: Indian Computer Emergency Response Team (CERT-In)
sections.mandatory_notes: Mandatory cybersecurity incident reporting to CERT-In within 6 hours of noticing incident.

sections.title: Punishment for sending offensive messages through communication service
sections.source: Shreya Singhal v. Union of India, (2015) 5 SCC 1 — struck down in entirety, 24 March 2015
sections.mandatory_notes: STRUCK DOWN: Unconstitutional under Article 19(1)(a). Invocation is legally prohibited and triggers an immediate GOVERNANCE BLOCK.

sections.title: Grounds for processing digital personal data
sections.mandatory_notes: Processing of personal data must be for lawful purpose with consent or legitimate use.

sections.title: General obligations of Data Fiduciary (security safeguards)
sections.mandatory_notes: Mandatory technical and organizational measures to prevent personal data breaches in investigation.

sections.title: Offence of money-laundering
sections.source: Prevention of Money Laundering Act, 2002 as amended
sections.mandatory_notes: Direct or indirect involvement in any process connected with proceeds of crime.

sections.title: Punishment for money-laundering
sections.source: Prevention of Money Laundering Act, 2002 as amended
sections.mandatory_notes: Prescribes rigorous imprisonment (3 to 7 years) and fine.
